historical_notes.body_markdown:
# Source and build-limit qualification

This is an independent research fixture, not a production replacement. It was run against GuavaJam `54fce07b619628a5e92be946be4b189873ddf1a0`, using Python 3.12.12, Git 2.56.1, locked GuavaJam dependencies, and Pandoc 3.12.1 where source validation was required. The shared source checkout was not edited.

## Measured findings

The 128-document and 100 MiB supporting-source guards can be removed without weakening the other tested source predicates. Removing those guards is insufficient to qualify large-work builds: the validator retains every AST, the renderer retains every HTML/source/navigation record, and cached builds hit another 1 MiB manifest ceiling.

| Fixture / operation | Stock | Experimental | Python peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Extract 4,000 tiny committed files | 31.976 s | 0.866 s, disk-backed path inventory | 24.36 MiB stock / 20.77 MiB experimental |
| Extract 16,000 tiny committed files | 96.285 s | 3.602 s, disk-backed path inventory | 31.58 MiB stock / 22.75 MiB experimental |
| Extract 260 MiB, 260 individually bounded blobs | Rejected at aggregate guard | 0.461 s; exact bytes verified | 20.14 MiB experimental |
| Validate 129 small supporting documents | Aggregate guard error only | Passed, 0.947 s | 24.63 MiB experimental |
| Validate 21 supporting documents, 105.0 MiB total | Aggregate guard error only | Passed, 36.391 s | 167.36 MiB experimental |
| Validate 4,000 small supporting documents | Not repeated | Passed, 30.877 s; renderer enumeration also passed | 43.01 MiB experimental |

Extraction results are one execution per scenario on a shared host, with no CPU throttling or cold-cache control. They measure Git snapshot extraction, not HTML generation or search. The 260 MiB fixture is highly compressible and not a semantically validated work. Timings stop at snapshot entry; byte/path verification and cleanup have separate total timings. Python RSS is not simultaneous process-tree RSS. The list-compatible batch variant still grows with path count: at 16,000 files it used 31.49 MiB, while the disk-backed iterable used 22.75 MiB.

`snapshot-results.json`, `guard-results.json`, and `guard-4000.json` retain exact measurements and environments.

## Cache ceiling reproduced

`cache_inventory_probe.py` exercises the real cache writer/reader, serializer, hash inventory, and renderer file naming with synthetic output. It avoids claiming a full rendered source corpus.

| Supporting documents | Manifest entries | CACHE.json bytes | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 128 | 387 | 39,680 | Accepted |
| 4,000 | 12,003 | 1,232,256 | Newly generated cache reported corrupt |
| 16,000 | 48,003 | 4,928,256 | Newly generated cache reported corrupt |

The production reader rejects `CACHE.json` above 1,048,576 bytes even though its writer emits that same inventory. The actual full renderer emits additional manuscript files, so the synthetic fixture is not an upper-bound estimate. Raising the supporting-document cap alone leaves this blocker.

## Extraction prototype

`bounded_snapshot.py` uses two Git processes: streamed `ls-tree -r -z`, then one in-flight blob request at a time through `cat-file --batch`. It spools the ordered path/object inventory to disk, validates each object header, streams blob bytes in 64 KiB pieces, and verifies the trailing framing newline. It keeps replacement objects/hooks/grafts out of object selection in the same way as the existing snapshot helper. It retains the 20 MiB individual blob limit, rejects nonregular Git entries, checks exact lowercase full SHA-1 identities and safe UTF-8 paths, uses exclusive file creation, and kills/reaps owned processes on errors or deadlines. Explicit operator file/total-byte budgets are supported independently of source validity.

The disk-backed iterable is not a drop-in promise of bounded memory throughout GuavaJam. Existing consumers still build sets, lists, AST dictionaries, and rendered inventories. A `retain_paths=True` adapter preserves the existing list-shaped test contract and demonstrates its O(document-count) memory cost.

The prototype introduces an 8 KiB tree-record bound solely for this experiment. It is not a proposed new publication-contract limit. POSIX process-group/selectors behavior, hostile concurrent filesystem replacement, cross-platform process handling, disk-full recovery, and the complete publication/archive/update lanes remain integration work.

## Correctness qualification

Fourteen targeted tests passed, covering raw selected bytes despite checkout/filter/export attributes and replacement refs; repeated disk-inventory iteration; symlink and submodule rejection; executable source treated as data; exact revision rejection; actual 20 MiB + 1 blob rejection; explicit operator budget boundaries; unsafe paths; wrong/missing blob headers; invalid framing; truncated streams; oversized headers; nonzero exits; and a stalled process deadline with cleanup. Six existing source-snapshot contracts passed through the list adapter.

The guard-only source copy produces identical errors to stock for unanchored material, nested metadata, an invalid supporting link, an oversized individual supporting document, and a symlink. `snapshot-correctness.json` and `guard-results.json` record these outcomes. These checks are targeted, not a claim that all source/publication or generator tests ran.

## Recommended implementation boundary

1. Remove the hard 128-document / 100 MiB supporting-source predicates from semantic source acceptance. Keep per-document parser/media/path/trust controls. Make finite build-work/disk/time budgets explicit trusted operator settings with actionable failures, never silent omission or metadata-controlled overrides.
2. Introduce one shared raw-Git batch reader rather than separate per-file subprocess loops. Keep full immutable identity, regular-file, byte-count, header/framing, deadline, cancellation and cleanup checks. A spool-backed inventory can bound extraction metadata if downstream APIs are adapted intentionally.
3. Validate in passes: parse one source item, retain compact anchors/outgoing references and other required facts in a disk-backed store, release the AST, then resolve every link against the exact edition inventory. A content parse cache must include parser/toolchain/source-policy identity and must not replace per-edition signature verification or cross-document checks.
4. Render each page and source/citation download into the existing private staging tree as it completes; retain hashes and compact descriptors rather than every output byte. Build NAV/VIEW/CACHE/SITE records incrementally or as bounded chunks plus a small root descriptor. Preserve exact inventory completeness and hash checks; update all readers/writers together. The private immutable view cache should retain bounded per-file/blob entries keyed by exact source and rendering context, while edition-specific navigation/citations remain occurrence-specific.
5. Feed normalized search rows from the same verified per-document records. Do not retain one giant NAV JSON or duplicate source-text copies merely to shuttle data between generators. Keep complete build accounting for temporary indexes, sort/vacuum scratch and atomically published artifacts.
6. Keep unrelated resource budgets scoped. Current 10,000 first-parent-commit discovery, 10,000-edition/16 MiB catalog, 1 MiB collection configuration, 256 repositories, 64 KiB metadata, and individual asset/parser guards are separate contracts/operations. A claim of unlimited history would require revisiting those paths too. In particular `MAX_HISTORY` counts first-parent commits, not just documentation editions. Do not silently lift all limits while changing document cardinality.

Complete signed rendering, cache reuse, no-op/update identity, archive restoration, full inventory verification, and browser/static-directory behavior at the target corpus size remain acceptance gates for the eventual integration commit. At least one large failure fixture should prove that the currently served generation survives budget exhaustion or cancellation.

## Reproduction

Use a disposable checkout of the exact baseline with its locked dependencies, and an actual Pandoc 3.12.1 binary. Set these task-specific environment variables when the checkout/tool locations differ:

```bash
export GUAVAJAM_REPO=/absolute/path/to/guavajam
export GUAVAJAM_PANDOC=/absolute/path/to/pandoc-3.12.1
python prepare_candidate.py
python test_bounded_snapshot.py
python measure_snapshots.py
python measure_guards.py
python measure_guards.py --worker candidate --case 4000-documents
python cache_inventory_probe.py
```

Run the scripts using the pinned checkout's Python/dependency environment. `prepare_candidate.py` copies source into this experiment directory and removes only the identified aggregate guard sites; it does not change the supplied checkout. Large fixtures are generated locally under `fixtures/` and need not be published. `aggregate-guard-only.patch` is experimental evidence, not the recommended complete production change.
